full_judgment:
19. The next point argued by the learned Advocate for the appellant is that the trial is vitiated for misjoinder of charges as both schedule and non-schedule offences are charged together. In support of his contention, he put reliance on the decision reported in 33, 35 and 31 DLR at pages 203, 127 and 174 respectively. The decision reported in 35 DLR 127 runs as follows: 

 20. The above decisions were referred to me at the time of deciding Criminal Appeal No. 471 of 1987 and after discussion of the same in the judgment of that case delivered on 4th April, 1990, I held that the offences which are made punishable both under the General Law and the Special law exclusively triable by the Special Tribunal under section 26 of the Special Powers Act 1974 cannot be said to be different offences and/or non-schedule offences, as those offences such as smuggling, and in the present case, selling women for prostitution, etc. have been made exclusively triable by the Special Tribunal and as such it cannot be said that the trial is vitiated by misjoinder of charges and the Special Tribunal had no jurisdiction to make charges of schedule and non-schedule offences. In the present case the accused was charged under sections 372/511 BPC and also sections 4 and 5 of the Cruelty to Women (Deterrent Punishment) Ordinance, 1983.
